speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked the Minister for Education when and how are salary scale and benefit reviews conducted and recommended for (i) educators from mainstream schools, preschools and special education schools and (ii) other staff such as education psychologists, job coach therapists and school leaders serving in these education institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Salary adjustments take into consideration the size of the salary gaps compared to market benchmarks.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Generally, larger adjustments are made when the gap with the market benchmarks is wider.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is in line with the principle that Civil Service salaries should keep pace with but not lead the market.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These adjustments also apply to MOE staff seconded to other agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Special Education (SPED) schools are run by Social Service Agencies (SSAs).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: While SPED schools receive full funding, SSAs retain substantial autonomy in HR practices, including how they compensate SPED school staff.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Nevertheless, MOE, in our role in overseeing the SPED sector, works closely with and supports the SSAs to ensure that salaries for SPED teachers remain competitive through periodic compensation reviews.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In 2018, salaries were reviewed together with the National Council of Social Service.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In 2020, salaries were again reviewed with the introduction of the Journeys of Excellence Package.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This Journeys package contains several complementary initiatives to raise the quality and professionalism of the SPED teaching profession by strengthening their competencies, expertise and career progression.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: MOE will continue to work with SSAs so that our SPED teachers have good career progression and updated salary guidelines.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For non-teaching SPED school staff such as psychologists, the SSAs take reference from the NCSS sector salary guidelines for different professions.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Recently, when the announcement for MOE teachers or Education Officers was made, it created quite a bit of ripple amongst the special education sector and also in the rest of the people sector where organisations take in students who graduate from the special schools.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: When announcements, such as this, are made unilaterally, it does affect the others.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Sometimes, the approach or the methodology by which these compensation reviews are made, are either not known or perhaps could be missed out when the original announcements were made.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I think it is always good and would MOE consider that when it makes announcements of such nature, especially in terms of compensation, that it be not announced unilaterally and that mention be made of the rest of the sector who are also serving the children, the young people or the older people of Singapore in education?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, that is one, that announcements will also make some mention of the rest of the service providers.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Number two, I would like MOE to consider and communicate to the SSAs – either special schools or disability organisations – the philosophy by which their salaries are computed or decided upon.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Because for some of the positions – such as the educators, psychologists, therapists and so forth – both sectors, the people and public sectors, are recruiting from the same pool.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The competitiveness is quite important because you want to serve such persons throughout their lifespan.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, the philosophy is quite important because they could be recruiting from the same pool.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I would appreciate that MOE would consider some of what I have shared.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I would say that, in general, we do this progressively, systematically and continuously.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The reason that we do not announce everything at one go is because we do the work in stages.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But every time we announce a change in one particular profession, we will certainly take into account the other professions to make sure that the relativities are maintained, both within the sector and also beyond the sector, with other professions.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the second comment, we will continue to share our methodologies of how this is done in the public sector with the people sector.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The methodology of how we compute the salaries and the remuneration packages – all this is not a secret.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We do it openly and there is an open methodology of how we do it.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will be very happy to share this with the rest of the SSAs.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is important that in every sector in the economy, we must allocate some of our top talents.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, even in preschools and SPED schools, are we allocating our top talents?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, is the Public Service Commission (PSC) offering scholarships to allow some of our top talents to be trained in those areas so that, in the future, they can lead the sectors?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, we cannot assume that the preschool teachers are of a lower level than the teachers in the Junior Colleges.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, in the long run, we must align the competencies, we must make sure that we recognise the competency level in every of these sectors and remunerate them accordingly.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We have heard a lot of stories that overseas, there are Masters and PhD holders becoming teachers of preschools, for example.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Sorry, Mr Leong Mun Wai, are you asking a question or are you —

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Specific to Mr Leong Mun Wai's question, Mr Leong might want to know or may already know that actually when I was in the Ministry of Social and Family Development, we have a talent development scheme working with the SSAs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Our aim is to make sure that they get a broader exposure so that the good ideas can spread around faster and the whole sector itself can benefit.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, we have been doing that and we will continue to do that.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On Mr Leong Mun Wai's second point about the salary structure, indeed, that is also what we have always been doing to make sure that every sector is compensated competitively.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Of course, we do not take compensation as the only reason to help people stay in the sector.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is also about career development, their route of advancement, the working environment and so forth.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But I would just like to raise one nuanced point.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I think we should be very careful about remunerating people based on credentials.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, whether educators have Masters, PhD or basic degree or diploma, I think we need to look at them, but we also need to look beyond that and look at the kind of skillsets that people have and the kind of contributions that people have made.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I would not say that just because someone has a Masters, therefore, they will obviously be paid more than someone who might be very experienced in the sector itself.
